page: Amazon Web Services r9gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture and powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. It features 64 dedicated physical cores running on 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64) at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, utilizing a single thread per core without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 512.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a balanced 8.0 GB of memory per core, which matches the characteristic 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of the AWS memory-optimized series.

The hardware configuration bundles 3800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside 34 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. There are no discrete GPUs included in this configuration. The integration of high-capacity local solid-state storage directly on the host server provides ultra-low latency input/output paths, bypassing external network-attached storage latency for scratch space, temporary table allocations, and transaction logging.

From an architectural standpoint, the ARM64 Graviton implementation offers strong operational efficiency per core relative to traditional x86-based memory instances, maximizing compute and memory density within a standard host footprint. The dedicated single-thread-per-core layout prevents resource contention between virtual threads, resulting in predictable compute performance across all 64 cores.

This server type is suitable for memory-heavy and disk-intensive enterprise workloads. Recommended deployments include in-memory databases, large Redis or Memcached distributed clusters, data analytics engines, distributed graph databases, and transactional relational database systems that benefit directly from high memory capacity coupled with fast local NVMe swap and temporary caching storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r9gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance engineered around AWS Graviton ARM64 architecture and the Nitro hypervisor. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz with one thread per core, paired with 512.0 GB of system memory to maintain an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Storage capabilities include a bundled 3800 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by a 34 Gbps baseline network interface, while operating without discrete GPU accelerators. The ARM-based processor design delivers consistent resource density and execution efficiency across large multi-core configurations without multithreading contention. By combining extensive memory capacity with fast local solid-state storage and dedicated high-bandwidth networking, the r9gd.16xlarge is engineered for demanding memory-bound applications, including distributed in-memory data grids, large-scale caching services, high-throughput transactional databases, and real-time analytical processing platforms requiring low-latency storage access.
